title: Browserless Pricing: Plans and Overage Costs (2026)
summary: Browserless pricing splits into four plans by concurrency: 2 on Free to 100 on Scale. Match your peak concurrency requirement to find the right plan.
body_markdown:
## Sending Browserless output into business apps with Activepieces


You still have a second problem once you know your session length and parallel jobs. Browserless gives you a browser that does the work, but it does nothing with what comes back.


A page capture or scraped table lands in the response and sits there until something picks it up.


Activepieces picks it up. It doesn't replace Browserless, and it doesn't make a browser run any cheaper or faster.


Its core is MIT-licensed, as the repository's LICENSE file on GitHub states, and the 742 integrations on the far side of the browser are counted directly from the` packages/pieces/community` folder of that same open-source monorepo, not taken from a marketing page.


What it does is run on a schedule, call the Browserless REST API through an HTTP step, and pass the result along to the places your team already looks.


In practice, a scheduler starts an Activepieces flow, the flow's HTTP step calls Browserless, and the result fans out to a spreadsheet that gains new rows, a PDF saved in a storage folder, and a Slack message.


The browser is one box in the middle, and everything on either side of it is plumbing you would otherwise build or do by hand.


### When a workflow tool fits and when it does not


It fits if your job is "every morning, grab this page, and get the answer to people who will never open a terminal." Without a tool like this, someone copies results into a sheet by hand, or the check simply stops happening the week that person is busy.


Skip the flow and you carry a recurring chore with a person attached; setting one up costs an afternoon.


It doesn't fit if you already run code. If a script of yours calls Browserless today, adding a row to a sheet or posting to Slack is a few more lines in that same script.


A second tool just gives you another place for things to break and another account to manage.


It also doesn't fix a bad plan choice. A flow that fires many Browserless calls at once still meets the same concurrency and session limits you sized earlier, so schedule jobs with that ceiling in mind.
